back_translation: Woe to the proud crown of the drunkards of Ephraim, to the fading flower of his glorious beauty, which adorns the hilltop above the fertile valley of those struck down by wine.
Behold, the Lord has one who is strong and mighty. Like a hailstorm and a tempest of destruction, like a storm of mighty overflowing waters, he will hurl that crown down to the ground with his hand.
The proud crown of the drunkards of Ephraim will be trampled underfoot.
And the fading flower of his glorious beauty, which adorns the hilltop above the fertile valley, will be like a fig ripe before summer: whoever sees it picks it into his hand and swallows it at once.
In that day the LORD of Hosts will be a beautiful crown and a glorious garland to the remnant of His people,
and a spirit of justice to the one who sits on the seat of judgment, and strength to those who drive the enemy back at the gate.

But these also stagger from wine and wander from strong drink: both priest and prophet stagger from strong drink; they are swallowed up by wine. They wander because of strong drink; they are dazed in seeing visions and stumble in rendering judgment.
For all the tables are full of filthy vomit; there is not a single clean place.
"Whom does he think he is teaching knowledge? To whom does he think he is explaining the message? To children just weaned from milk? To infants just taken from the breast?
For it is just: 'Command upon command, command upon command, line upon line, line upon line, a little here, a little there.'"
Therefore He will speak to this people with stammering lips and with the tongue of foreigners,
He who said to them: "This is the rest — let the weary rest in peace; and this is the refreshing repose." But they were not willing to listen.

So the word of the LORD will become to them: "Command upon command, command upon command, line upon line, line upon line, a little here, a little there," so that they will go and fall backward, and be broken to pieces, and be snared and captured.
Therefore, you scoffers who rule this people in Jerusalem, hear the word of the LORD.

For you have said, "We have made a covenant with death, and we have made an agreement with the realm of the dead. When the overwhelming scourge passes through, it will not reach us, for we have made a lie our refuge, and we have hidden ourselves in falsehood."

Therefore the Lord GOD says this: "Behold, I lay a stone in Zion as a foundation, a stone that has been tested, a precious cornerstone, a firm foundation; the one who believes will not panic and flee.
And I will make justice the measuring line and righteousness the plumb line. Hail will sweep away the refuge of lies, and water will flood the hiding place.
Your covenant with death will be annulled, and your agreement with the realm of the dead will not stand. When the overwhelming scourge passes through, you will be trampled down by it.

Every time it passes through, it will sweep you away too, for it will pass through morning after morning, by day and by night; and when this message is understood, there will be nothing but sheer terror.
For the bed is too short to stretch out on, and the blanket too narrow to wrap around oneself.
For the LORD will rise up as at Mount Perazim; He will rouse Himself as in the Valley of Gibeon, to do His work — His strange work — and to perform His task — His alien task.
Therefore, now, scoff no more, or your chains will grow heavier; for I have heard from the Lord GOD of Hosts a decreed destruction upon the whole land.
Give ear and hear my voice; pay attention and hear my words.
Does the plowman plow the soil to sow every day? Does he keep on opening and harrowing his ground forever?
When he has leveled its surface, does he not scatter black cumin and sow cumin? He plants wheat in rows, barley in its plot, and spelt along the border of his field.
For his God instructs him in the right method; He teaches him.
For black cumin is not threshed with a threshing sledge, and a cart wheel is not rolled over cumin; but black cumin is beaten out with a staff, and cumin with a rod.
Grain for bread must be ground, but no one threshes it forever; though he rolls his cart wheel over it, his horses do not crush it to powder.
This also comes from the LORD of Hosts. He makes His counsel wonderful, and He makes His wisdom great and excellent.
